transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: To be transparent, I don’t have a verified rental-yield figure or substantiated appreciation forecast to quote, so I wouldn’t want to promise a percentage. What I can confirm is that the current Type A 900 sq.ft. one-carpark package starts from RM302,000; exact pricing depends on floor, facing, car-park allocation and package applicability. That’s an entry-price reference, not an investment-return estimate. What budget range and holding period are you considering?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Looking at around RM300k, probably a 5–7 year hold. I’d need the net numbers to make sense, not just gross yield—especially maintenance, sinking fund, vacancy and phase supply. Is the RM0.18 psf inclusive of sinking fund, and what’s the source for that figure?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: You’re right to focus on net numbers. The RM0.18 psf figure is stated in Pearlmont’s latest project FAQ, updated 17 September 2026, as inclusive of the sinking fund. For a 900 sq.ft. unit, that is RM162 per month at the stated rate. It covers the stated maintenance rate only—not vacancy, rental assumptions or phase-supply risk—and I still don’t have a verified rental-yield forecast to quote.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Okay, thanks for clarifying the source and that there’s no verified yield forecast. For my 5–7 year hold, can you share the phase-wise unit supply and any actual rental evidence or comparable transactions? I’m comparing this against a few other projects, so I’d rather underwrite it conservatively than assume the facilities will drive demand.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Okay, stress-test it using RM1,500 and RM1,700 rent, with vacancy allowance and the RM162 monthly maintenance. Please show the net yield range clearly, and flag any costs you’re not able to verify. If the numbers still look reasonable, I can consider a viewing after that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Using the RM302,000 entry reference and assuming a 5% vacancy allowance: at RM1,500 rent, annual rent after vacancy is RM17,100; less RM1,944 annual maintenance gives RM15,156 net before other costs, or about 5.0% net yield. At RM1,700 rent, the equivalent is RM17,436, or about 5.8%. This excludes financing, assessment/quit rent, insurance, repairs, furnishing, agent fees, tax and transaction costs, which I can’t verify here. So this is an assumption-based sensitivity range, not Pearlmont rental evidence or a forecast. If that range is still workable for your comparison, viewing the actual layout would be the next useful step.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: The 5.0%–5.8% assumption-based range looks potentially workable, but I’m treating it as a sensitivity only since several costs are still unverified. I’m open to a viewing to check the actual layout and location—what weekday or weekend slots are available?

transcript.speaker: agent

judge.summary: Yes. With reliable Human Support, the AI can use verified answers to continue selling and move a suitable buyer toward Appointment Ready. The appointment was not confirmed because no specific available slot was supplied.
judge.improvement_recommendation: Deduplicate resolved support requests and reuse the existing verified result directly; otherwise preserve the current honest investment-selling flow.
